issues.label: Correct statute version applied
issues.why: Court must apply the ORS 609.035 version in effect at trial, not the 2025 amendment.

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must have jurisdiction over the charged misdemeanor/violation and location.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must have jurisdiction over defendant based on proper appearance/service.

issues.label: Valid charging instrument
issues.why: Complaints/informations must allege every element of ORS 609.035 for each count.

issues.label: Duplicity/uncertainty in counts
issues.why: Court must ensure each count charges one offense and is sufficiently definite as to dog/victim/time/place.

issues.label: Two-count unit of prosecution
issues.why: Court must decide whether two counts properly lie (e.g., per dog kept, per dog-inflicting-injury, or per incident) and avoid improper multiplication.

issues.label: Merger of guilty findings
issues.why: If statutory unit is not per-dog, convictions may need merger into one judgment.

issues.label: Double jeopardy considerations
issues.why: Court must ensure multiple convictions/punishments do not violate state/federal double jeopardy.

issues.label: Pro se waiver validity
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant knowingly waived counsel (or properly declined) and understood risks.

issues.label: Jury trial waiver validity
issues.why: Court must ensure jury waiver was knowing, voluntary, and on the record.

issues.label: Bench-trial factfinder role
issues.why: Court must act as neutral factfinder and apply correct burdens and standards.

issues.label: Burden of proof applied
issues.why: State must prove every element beyond a reasonable doubt; court must not shift burden on provocation/right-to-exclude.

issues.label: Elements of ORS 609.035 identified
issues.why: Court must correctly identify each statutory element the state must prove.

issues.label: Keeper status proved
issues.why: State must prove defendant was the “keeper” of each dog charged.

issues.label: Dog identity per count
issues.why: State must prove which dog(s) constitute each charged dangerous dog count (Moki vs Gyptian).

issues.label: Prior qualifying conviction element
issues.why: If ORS 609.035 requires a prior nuisance/potentially-dangerous-dog conviction, court must find it proved and qualifying.

issues.label: Proof of prior conviction admissibility
issues.why: Court must ensure prior conviction evidence is properly authenticated and admissible for the element.

issues.label: Prior conviction constitutional validity
issues.why: If challenged, court may need to consider whether prior conviction can be used (e.g., uncounseled conviction limits).

issues.label: Physical injury to domestic animal
issues.why: Court must determine Baby Girl is a “domestic animal” and that “physical injury” occurred as defined/understood in the statute.

issues.label: Causation by defendant’s dogs
issues.why: State must prove defendant’s dog(s) caused the injury, including factual and legal causation.

issues.label: Injury attribution between dogs
issues.why: For two counts, court must decide whether each dog inflicted injury or whether liability attaches even if only one bit.

issues.label: Without provocation element
issues.why: Court must decide whether Baby Girl provoked the attack under ORS 609.035’s meaning.

issues.label: Definition of provocation
issues.why: Court must determine the legal standard for “provocation” (objective/subjective; by victim animal; immediacy).

issues.label: Provocation evidentiary conflict
issues.why: Court must resolve conflicting accounts (Gaul/Shoesmith vs McCrery) regarding barking/nipping/biting through fence.

issues.label: Location element satisfied
issues.why: Court must decide whether the injury occurred at a place where defendant had no lawful right to exclude others.

issues.label: Where incident began vs occurred
issues.why: If statute turns on where the injury occurred, court must not substitute a “began” standard unless statute supports it.

issues.label: Public path legal status
issues.why: Court must determine whether the path outside the fence was public right-of-way/easement and open to the public.

issues.label: Property boundary and right-to-exclude
issues.why: Court must determine the boundary line and whether Gaul was on premises defendant could lawfully exclude from.

issues.label: Effect of dog dragged into yard
issues.why: Court must determine whether element is satisfied if attack starts outside and continues inside defendant’s yard.

issues.label: Trespass/implied license issues
issues.why: If Gaul entered yard to intervene, court must assess whether defendant could lawfully exclude him at that moment and whether it matters.

issues.label: Criminal negligence element
issues.why: Court must decide whether defendant acted with criminal negligence as required (if ORS 609.035 so requires).

issues.label: Risk awareness standard applied
issues.why: Court must apply ORS 161.085(10) gross-deviation standard to fence/gate security and foreseeability.

issues.label: Evidence of fence condition
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether makeshift barrier/broken boards show substantial unjustifiable risk of escape/attack.

issues.label: Foreseeability from prior incident
issues.why: Prior nuisance/potentially-dangerous-dog conviction may bear on foreseeability and negligence and must be weighed properly.

issues.label: Unlawful propensity inference limits
issues.why: Court must ensure prior attack evidence is used for permissible purposes (element/mental state) and not pure character propensity.

issues.label: ORS 403 balancing
issues.why: Court must consider undue prejudice vs probative value of prior conviction and other inflammatory evidence.

issues.label: Relevance of decorative fence photos
issues.why: Court must decide whether defendant’s photos meaningfully rebut state’s theory and how much weight to give them.

issues.label: Witness credibility findings
issues.why: Court must make rational credibility determinations and avoid relying on improper factors.

issues.label: Sufficiency of evidence standard
issues.why: Court must ensure evidence supports each element beyond reasonable doubt when viewed as a whole.

issues.label: Inconsistent witness accounts
issues.why: Court must resolve inconsistencies (who initiated, how fence broke, whether Baby Girl bit Zorro) and still meet burden.

issues.label: Defense theories considered
issues.why: Court must consider defendant’s provocation and “Baby Girl stuck in fence” theories and whether they create reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Self-defense/defense of animal
issues.why: Court must consider whether any statutory/common-law justification (dogs defending Zorro) negates “without provocation” or culpability.

issues.label: Intervening acts causation
issues.why: Court must consider whether Gaul entering yard or other acts break causal chain or affect location/provocation analysis.

issues.label: Variance from state’s opening
issues.why: Court must ensure proof at trial matches charged theory (e.g., “pulled into yard”) without prejudicial variance.

issues.label: Findings for each count
issues.why: Court must make clear, count-specific findings (each dog, each element) to support two convictions.

issues.label: Sentencing authority and limits
issues.why: If conviction, court must impose lawful sentence and conditions under ORS chapter 609 and general sentencing statutes.

issues.label: Collateral dog-control orders
issues.why: Court must consider any mandatory/permissive orders (confinement, muzzle, licensing, euthanasia, restitution) triggered by conviction.

issues.label: Restitution eligibility
issues.why: If sought, court must determine whether veterinary costs are economic damages and supported by evidence.

issues.label: Due process for pro se
issues.why: Court must ensure defendant had meaningful opportunity to present evidence, cross-examine, and understand procedures.

issues.label: Evidentiary foundation for photos
issues.why: Court must ensure photos of injuries and fence were properly authenticated and relevant.

issues.label: Hearsay concerns
issues.why: Court must exclude or properly admit any out-of-court statements offered for truth (e.g., prior incident details).

issues.label: Scope of judicial notice
issues.why: If court relied on property/public-path facts, it must ensure proper proof or permissible judicial notice.

issues.label: Mens rea per element
issues.why: Court must match the required mental state (if any) to each element and not assume strict liability.

issues.label: Constitutional vagueness concerns
issues.why: If raised, court must consider whether “provocation” or “lawful right to exclude” is unconstitutionally vague as applied.

issues.label: Sufficiency re ‘lawful exclude’
issues.why: Court must ensure evidence establishes defendant lacked lawful right to exclude others from the specific location at relevant time.
